Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge along with other leaders pay tribute to Dr BR Ambedkar on Constitution Day, at the Ambedkar Mahasabha, in Lucknow, on November 26, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI
C ongress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the people of Uttar Pradesh had taught the BJP a lesson in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘400 paar’ slogan into silence.
Addressing a ‘Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan’ at the Congress office in Lucknow, he also alleged that inflation, unemployment, prices of LPG, and food items were rising, while the BJP’s coffers were filling up.
Mr. Kharge thanked the people of Uttar Pradesh for checking the BJP’s electoral ambitions and said Modi, who had repeatedly invoked the ‘400 paar’ slogan during the campaign, was now “sitting quietly”.
“I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, ‘Abki Baar, 400 Paar’ (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today,” Mr. Kharge said.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 26, 2026), led the nation, in greeting all fellow citizens on the occasion of Constitution Day and said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India.
Also read: Why is November 26 celebrated as Constitution Day in India
Constitution Day, also known as ‘Samvidhan Divas’, is celebrated in the country on November 26 every year to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India.
On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India, which came into effect from January 26, 1950. The Modi government in 2015 notified its decision to celebrate November 26 every year as Constitution Day to promote the values of the foundational document among citizens.
Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan called for respecting all languages and cautioned against looking down upon other people’s mother tongues, saying that respect for one’s own language must go hand in hand with respect for the languages of others.
“If I don’t respect the sentiments of others, then I don’t deserve that my sentiments will be respected by others,” Mr. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that linguistic diversity should be a source of mutual respect and national unity.
Addressing an event organised by the Union Law Ministry to mark the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution, he released its updated versions in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
Describing the initiative as a celebration of India’s linguistic diversity and democratic inclusiveness, the Vice-President said making the Constitution available in different languages would bring governance closer to the people and enable citizens to understand the country’s foundational document in their mother tongues.
“Our Constitution is our pride and our duty,” he said, adding that the availability of the document in multiple languages reflected the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and the collective responsibility of citizens in upholding constitutional values.
He also cautioned against equating knowledge with proficiency in English, saying it was just another language like any Indian mother tongue.
“Never think that speaking in English is knowledge. English is also one of the languages like our mother tongue. It’s nothing more,” he said.
“If our nation is not protected, none of our languages will be protected,” he said, urging citizens to work with the spirit of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First). — PTI
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Opposition parties on Thursday (November 26, 2026) of weakening the Constitution and democratic institutions, saying those who had attempted to “strangle the Constitution” when in power were now carrying a red book to mislead people.
He criticised Congress for “disrespecting Ambedkar”, and alleged that the party did not confer the Bharat Ratna on him and conspired to prevent him from entering Parliament.
Addressing a Constitution Day programme at the Lok Bhavan auditorium in Lucknow, Mr. Adityanath said India’s sovereignty did not belong to any individual, family or particular caste but rested with the common citizens of the country.
“Those who tried to strangle the Constitution when they had the opportunity are today carrying a red book and misleading the people,” he said in an apparent attack on Congress. The chief minister also launched beautification works at 3,955 sites housing statues of Dr B R Ambedkar and other social reformers under the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme.
He administered a collective oath on the Preamble of the Constitution along with Deputy Chief Ministers and other dignitaries. Adityanath said 4,030 sites associated with Ambedkar and other champions of social justice had been identified across the state, of which work would begin at 3,955 locations.
The sites would be equipped with facilities such as canopies, boundary walls, CCTV cameras, security arrangements and gardens, depending on requirements, the chief minister said. -- PTI
The Union Health Ministry on Thursday (November 26, 2026) observed Constitution Day with its officers collectively reading the Preamble to the Constitution and reaffirming their commitment to its values and ideals.
The programme was held at the Kartavya Bhawan here, with senior officers, including additional secretaries, joint secretaries, directors and deputy secretaries of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, participating.
Officials from the National AIDS Control Organisation, National Health Authority and National Medical Commission, among others, joined the programme through video conferencing, the ministry said in a statement.
The observance provided an opportunity for officials to reaffirm their collective commitment to the constitutional values that guide India’s democratic framework and governance, it said. -- PTI
Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the state is inhabited by 36 communities, and that all communities should work collectively to strengthen the bonds of love and unity, as enshrined in the Constitution.
Speaking at a function organised on the occasion of the Samvidhan Diwas at the Civil Secretariat in Mantripukhri area in Imphal, the Chief Minsiter said every person residing in the state must identify themselves “first as an Indian and secondly as a Manipuri”.
He also urged the people to collectively resolve to uphold the spirit of the Preamble of the Constitution and work towards a “society based on justice, liberty, equality and fraternity”.
“Manipur is inhabited by 36 communities, and all communities should work collectively to further strengthen the bonds of love and unity, as enshrined in the Preamble to the Constitution. Every individual residing in the state must identify themselves, first as an Indian and secondly as a Manipuri,” Mr. Singh said. -- PTI
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the people of Uttar Pradesh had taught the BJP a lesson in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘400 paar’ slogan into silence.
Addressing a ‘Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan’ at the Congress office in Lucknow, he also alleged that inflation, unemployment, prices of LPG, and food items were rising, while the BJP’s coffers were filling up.
Mr. Kharge thanked the people of Uttar Pradesh for checking the BJP’s electoral ambitions and said Modi, who had repeatedly invoked the ‘400 paar’ slogan during the campaign, was now “sitting quietly”.
“I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, ‘Abki Baar, 400 Paar’ (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today,” Mr. Kharge said.
The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) had won 36 of Uttar Pradesh’s 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections.
He also claimed that Union Home Minister Amit Shah had reduced his public statements, adding, “I do not know whether the two (Modi and Shah) are getting along or not.”
Taking a veiled jibe at Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Kharge said another leader in Lucknow also had his eyes on the prime minister’s chair. -- PTI
The Odisha Assembly observed Constitution Day, with Speaker Surama Padhy administering a pledge to members, including Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, to uphold the values enshrined in the Constitution.
Legislators gathered at the main entrance of the Assembly Hall, where Padhy read the Preamble, which the others collectively followed.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said political agendas of lawyers must not be masqueraded as professional duties, nor should judicial platforms be targeted for personal gains.
“Disagreement is not a weakness of constitutional democracy. A strong Bar must be able to question, challenge and disagree. Equally, a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority. What matters is that such engagement must remain guided by reason, professional integrity and respect for constitutional processes,” CJI Surya Kant said in his address at the Constitutional Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association.
“If political agendas are masqueraded as professional duty or judicial platforms are targeted for personal gains – there stands the professional integrity impaired,” he added.
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary urged people to uphold the core values of the Constitution, including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, saying it is not merely the foundation of the country’s governance system but also the guardian of every citizen’s rights, duties and dignity.
In a post on X on the occasion of Constitution Day, Mr. Choudhary said the Constitution strengthens India’s democratic traditions and inspires the nation to preserve its unity and integrity.
“Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country’s system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen’s rights, duties and dignity,” the CM said.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday (November 26, 2026) announced the launch of beautification works under the ‘Dr B R Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme’ on Constitution Day and said the initiative reflected his government’s commitment to the ideals of the architect of the Constitution.
He also said that Samajwadi Party leaders have left no stone unturned in hurting the self-respect of marginalised sections through inappropriate remarks about Ambedkar and his memorials, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi had developed five important places associated with Ambedkar’s life as ‘Panchteerth’ and given global recognition to his thoughts and legacy.
In a post on X, Mr. Adityanath said, “On the auspicious occasion of Constitution Day, beautification works are going to be launched today under the Dr B R Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme. This initiative symbolises our government’s unwavering commitment to the thoughts, ideals and social justice envisioned by Bharat Ratna Baba Saheb Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar.”
He said a true tribute to Ambedkar would be to imbibe his values and work towards building the egalitarian society he had envisioned.
“With this ideological commitment, and under the guidance of the prime minister, the double-engine government is making the basic spirit of the Constitution the foundation of governance and giving priority to the deprived,” Adityanath said.
“Ensuring dignity, equal opportunities and the benefits of development for the person standing at the last rung of society is our government’s resolve,” he added. -- PTI
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday (November 26, 2026) hailed the Constitution as the soul of India and pledged to defend it under all circumstances.
In a post on X on Constitution Day, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha (LoP) said it is the foundation of our democracy and a weapon against injustice.
“India’s Constitution is not just a book; it is the soul of the nation. It is a shield for every citizen’s dignity, the strength of every voice, a guardian of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity,” he said in his post, further calling it “our greatest weapon against injustice”.
“On Constitution Day, I renew my pledge; we will defend it under all circumstances and keep fighting for every Indian’s rights. Long live the Constitution, long live India!” the LoP asserted.
Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge also gave his best wishes to fellow citizens on Constitution Day and reaffirmed his pledge to save it along with democracy.
“Political democracy cannot survive unless there is social democracy at its foundation,” he said in a post on X, quoting Dr B R Ambedkar.
“Heartfelt wishes to all fellow citizens on Constitution Day,” he said while giving salutations to Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Azad, Dr Rajendra Prasad, Sarojini Naidu, Ambedkar and all the great national leaders who laid the foundation of modern India.
“Today, protecting the Constitution’s core ideals — justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, secularism and socialism — is our greatest national responsibility. Let us renew our pledge to protect the Constitution and democracy and preserve the country’s unity, integrity, and harmony. Victory to India. Victory to the Constitution,” Mr. Kharge said in his post.
The Congress has organised protests against “vote chori” across the country to mark the day. -- PTI
BSP chief Mayawati on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the mission of B R Ambedkar to empower Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other marginalised sections will remain incomplete as long as they don’t hold the “master key” of political power in their own hands.
The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister urged the Bahujan community to introspect why political power at the Centre remained beyond its reach despite the country having been independent for decades and adopting a Constitution drafted under Ambedkar’s leadership.
“The mission of B R Ambedkar to empower Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other marginalised sections remained incomplete as long as they did not hold the master key of political power in their own hands,” she said on X.
Referring to Ambedkar’s message that “political power is the master key” that opens all doors to progress and development, Mayawati questioned whether successive governments at the Centre had honestly fulfilled their constitutional responsibilities, particularly with regard to reservation, poverty, unemployment, education, healthcare and self-respect.
She said the community should demand accountability from governments if they had failed to discharge these responsibilities.
Recalling Ambedkar’s concluding address in the Constituent Assembly ahead of the formal adoption of the Constitution on November 26, 1949, Ms. Mayawati said he had warned against caste divisions and stressed the need to abandon casteism and take concrete steps to transform India from a country into a nation. -- PTI
Prime Minister Narendra Modi asserted that no force can stop the delivery of justice to women and blamed “one opposition party” for the defeat in Parliament of a delimitation-linked Constitution amendment bill, giving 33% reservation to women.
In a signed article that appeared in major newspapers on Thursday (November 26, 2026), Mr. Modi, without naming the Congress, also claimed that the biggest party in the Opposition wants to reduce OBC reservation and bring Muslim reservations.
“The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame,” he said.
The Prime Minister said a legislation aimed at giving women adequate representation in legislative bodies was disallowed from being passed by one opposition party, once again showing its “disdain for constitutional values”.
“I assure the ‘Nari Shakti’ of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he said.
Mr. Modi said Indian constitutional democracy has a clearly defined role for the Opposition.
“Sadly, the leading opposition party seems to have become more of an ‘Avrodh Paksh’ (obstructionist) than a ‘Virodh Paksh’ (opposition),” he said. -- PTI
Arunachal Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein also extended his greetings, urging people to reflect on the ideals and vision of the Constitution’s framers.
The Constitution continues to guide the nation and strengthen the foundations of democracy, he said.
“As we uphold the principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, let us renew our commitment to serving the people, respecting our institutions and contributing towards a stronger, inclusive and progressive India,” Mr. Mein said. -- PTI
Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu on Thursday (November 26, 2026) greeted the people of the state on Constitution Day, recalling the contributions of BR Ambedkar and other members of the Constituent Assembly in shaping the country’s Constitution.
In a social media post, Mr. Khandu said the occasion was an opportunity to remember the vision and collective wisdom of the Constitution’s framers, whose efforts laid the foundation of the republic and continue to guide India’s democratic journey.
“My warmest greetings to all on Constitution Day. Today, we remember Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and the members of the Constituent Assembly whose collective vision and wisdom laid the foundation of our Republic,” he said.
Describing the Constitution as the guiding spirit of Indian democracy, Mr. Khandu said it continued to uphold the fundamental values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, which remain central to the country’s democratic system. -- PTI
Ahead of their ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally in Nagpur, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka visited Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Speaking to the media after visiting Deekshabhoomi, Dipke said, “Today is a very holy day for everyone in the country because, on this day, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar gave us the Constitution, on which our country is running and moving forward.”
Dipke said he wanted to begin the day by paying his respects to Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar at Deekshabhoomi on this sacred occasion.
Deekshabhoomi is a Buddhist monument and pilgrimage site in Nagpur, commemorating the conversion of Ambedkar and hundreds of thousands of his followers to Buddhism on October 14, 1956.
The CJP leader said that they would participate in the ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally at 4 pm, which would also be attended by Ranka and actor Prakash Raj. -- PTI
On November 26, 2026, India marks 77 years since the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution in 1949. That founding charter made a bold promise for a poor, deeply stratified country emerging from colonial rule. Every adult citizen, regardless of property, caste, gender, or creed, would stand equal at the ballot box. Today, that core principle of political democracy, which B.R. Ambedkar placed at the heart of the Republic, is being systematically erased in practice.
Every November 26, on Constitution Day in India, a striking visual emerges on the political landscape. Opposition leaders, civil rights activists, and citizens step into the public space clutching pocket-sized editions of the Constitution of India — often bound in bright red. Waving these slender volumes is a powerful symbolic gesture that signals a collective resolve to defend the Republic against majoritarian consolidation and the erosion of democratic norms.
If the defenders of India’s republic wish to halt the march of ethno-religious nationalism, they must take constitutional values beyond academic discussions and bring them to ordinary people
On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted our Constitution. Today, we remember Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, and every member of the Constituent Assembly. Their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution.
For a nation as diverse as Bharat, with its numerous faiths, languages, customs, and schools of thought, it is important that the Constitution has a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Our endeavour has been to deepen its connect with the collective consciousness of our people, especially our youth and strengthen the spirit of unity essential to India’s bright future. That is why over a decade ago, our government decided to mark November 26 as Constitution Day.

Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas, is observed every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949 by the Constituent Assembly.
The Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950, two months later, making India a republic. However, November 26 is celebrated as the Constitution Day to commemorate the moment the Constitution of India was formally adopted for “We, the People of India”.
Constitution Day in India marks the 1949 adoption of the Preamble and Constitution, commemorating people’s sovereignty and democratic values.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 26, 2026) highlighted the Constitution’s role in strengthening democracy and promoting social and economic justice, while outlining his government’s achievements through welfare schemes and constitutional amendments. He said collective efforts guided by “India First” thinking, duties in action and constitutional values would realise Viksit Bharat by 2047.
PM Modi highlights Constitution’s role in democracy, justice, and inclusive welfare schemes, urging unity and youth engagement for a developed India by 2047.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the Constitution is not merely a legal framework but a “living sacred document” that safeguards justice, liberty, equality and fraternity for every citizen.
In a social media post on the occasion of Constitution Day, Sarma recalled the contributions of the members of the Constituent Assembly who laid the foundation of the country’s vibrant democracy.
The Constitution empowers institutions, guarantees fundamental rights and reminds citizens of their duties towards nation-building, he said.
“As we march forward in this Amrit Kaal, let us reaffirm our collective commitment to upholding constitutional values, strengthening the nation’s unity and serving the motherland with an unwavering dedication,” he added. -- PTI
Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Thursday (November 26, 2026) greeted the people on Constitution Day, reaffirming the importance of upholding the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
In a message posted on X, Mr Sinha said the Constitution stands as the supreme guiding light of India’s democracy and enshrines its timeless values.
“Greetings on Constitution Day. Our Constitution stands as the supreme guiding light of our democracy, enshrining the timeless values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity,” he said.
He called upon people to reaffirm their commitment to upholding these ideals and fulfilling their fundamental duties to build a stronger and Viksit Bharat. -- PTI
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 26, 2026) greeted all fellow citizens on the occasion of Constitution Day and said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India.
Mr. Modi also said that it is a day to pay homage to the makers of the Constitution and an occasion to reaffirm the commitment to strengthening the values enshrined in it.
“Warmest greetings on Constitution Day to all fellow citizens,” he said in a social media post. -- PTI
Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) chief Prakash Ambedkar on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) warned that the country could face a “blood revolution” unless the Constitution is saved and people are allowed to choose their own representatives.
Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, held ahead of Constitution Day, Mr. Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power.
Prakash Ambedkar warns of a potential “blood revolution” unless India’s Constitution is protected amid alleged RSS/BJP threats and North-South divides.
